note: Recorded sample output for demos and tests, written for the invoice-reconciliation sample brief.

output.summary: A focused, keyboard-friendly design that puts the exceptions first and keeps a full audit trail. Three things must be fixed before release: automatic matches are explained by a confidence score instead of a rule, differences in the evidence rely on colour alone, and submitting a resolution is a dead end for keyboard users.
strengths: Exceptions is the home page, and every exception says why it was flagged, naming the rule and both values
Invoice, purchase order and payment sit side by side, so the comparison happens on one screen
Second-person approval is built in, and self-approval is blocked with a plain explanation
Import keeps valid rows and lists rejected ones with a specific reason for each
Every loading state is announced and every error state has a way forward

findings.title: Automatic matches are explained by a confidence score
findings.detail: Controllers spot-checking matches and auditors sampling them can't tell what was compared, so they can't accept the match without redoing it. The brief requires every automatic decision to be explainable, and the deck's own principle is 'Explain, don't assert'.
findings.evidence: 'Why these were matched' shows 'Matched automatically · 98% confidence' (matches.why-summary). It doesn't name the rule, its version, the fields compared or the tolerance.
findings.recommendation: Replace the score with the rule and version, a field-by-field comparison (same / within tolerance) and the tolerance applied, e.g. 'Matched by rule R2, version 3' and 'Amount differs by £1.60. Rule R2 allows up to £5.00.' Add 'confidence' and 'score' to the words to avoid.

findings.title: Differences in the evidence are shown by colour alone
findings.detail: People with colour-vision deficiencies, and anyone printing or using high-contrast mode, can't see which value is wrong, which is the whole point of this screen.
findings.evidence: The evidence row's note says values that differ are shown in the danger colour; the invoice card's 'Quantity 120' and 'Total £1,440.00' have no icon or text marking them as different. The deck's 'Differs' label (exception-detail.diff-label) isn't used.
findings.recommendation: Mark each differing value with a warning icon and the 'Differs' label, plus the size of the difference ('20 more than received'). Keep the colour as a secondary cue.

findings.title: Submitting a resolution is a dead end for keyboard users
findings.detail: AP specialists work through dozens of exceptions in a row. Going back to the top of the queue and finding their place again on every item breaks the keyboard flow the research says they rely on.
findings.heuristic: H7 Flexibility and efficiency of use
findings.evidence: The confirmation's only action is 'Back to exceptions' as the primary button; 'Next exception' isn't offered and the focus target isn't specified.
findings.recommendation: Make 'Next exception' the primary action on the confirmation and move focus to it, with 'Back to exceptions' as a tertiary action.

findings.title: Side navigation hides how much is waiting
findings.detail: A reviewer working elsewhere can't see that nine resolutions are waiting until they open Approvals.
findings.evidence: The side navigation lists Exceptions and Approvals without counts; the numbers only appear in the stats on Exceptions.
findings.recommendation: Show counts next to Exceptions and Approvals in the side navigation, with an accessible name such as 'Approvals, 9 waiting'.

findings.title: The exception queue can't be sorted
findings.detail: At month-end, AP specialists triage by value first (research persona behaviour); without a sort they fall back to filters or the spreadsheet.
findings.heuristic: H7 Flexibility and efficiency of use
findings.evidence: The queue is fixed to oldest first; there is no sort control for amount or age.
findings.recommendation: Add a sort control (oldest first, largest amount first) and remember the choice per person.

findings.title: Amounts don't line up
findings.detail: Comparing amounts down a list is slower when digits don't align.
findings.evidence: The theme names tabular figures as a principle, but no type style sets them, and amounts sit at the end of list rows rather than in an aligned column.
findings.recommendation: Set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on the body, label and headline styles used for amounts, and right-align amounts in their own column.

findings.title: Single-key shortcuts on Approvals need a focus condition
findings.detail: If the keys are global, a stray keystroke or a speech-input command could approve a resolution. The fix is to extend the pattern Exceptions already uses.
findings.evidence: Exceptions says shortcuts work only while the list has focus, but Approvals ('A approves · R sends back') and Exception ('J opens the next exception') don't say when the keys are active.
findings.recommendation: Make single-key shortcuts active only while the list or the selected resolution has focus, and add a setting to turn them off.

heuristicsReviewed.note: Matches are explained by a score rather than a rule (C1); the navigation hides waiting counts (C4).

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H2 Match between system and the real world
heuristicsReviewed.note: Accounting terms (PO, short-pay, credit note) and rule names users can trace.
Unmatch and send back are always available; nothing is final until a second person approves.
One side navigation, consistent page headers and one primary action per state.
Self-approval is blocked; rows are checked on import before anything is matched.
Evidence and reasons are on screen; nothing has to be remembered between pages.

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H7 Flexibility and efficiency of use
heuristicsReviewed.note: Confirmation after submitting breaks the keyboard flow (C3); the queue can't be sorted (C5).
Dense but ordered: evidence, then decision, then actions.

heuristicsReviewed.heuristic: H9 Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors
heuristicsReviewed.note: Import errors name the file, the row and the reason, and say how to fix them.
Shortcut hints on every queue; Matching rules documents the rules behind matches.

wcagChecked.note: Lists, labels and headings are structured; evidence cards have headings.
Differences in the evidence rely on colour alone (C2).
All text pairs meet 4.5:1 in light and dark mode (design-system check).
Borders and focus ring reach 3:1 against their backgrounds.
Every queue, filter and action is reachable by keyboard.
Focus condition for single-key shortcuts isn't specified on Approvals and Exception (C7).
Focus after submitting a resolution isn't specified (C3).
2 px focus ring defined for every interactive component, including list rows.
32 px minimum target, above the 24 px requirement.
Field and import errors are described in text next to the item.
Icon buttons carry text; rows have full accessible names; chips expose selected state.
Loading text is announced; confirmations use role=status.
